title: Define the four-lens review and final approval workflow
description: Design built-in review expectations for people, reader agents, search crawlers and social previews. Determine what evidence, findings, unresolved risks and editorial judgment the final review presents, what happens when a lens cannot be assessed, and how this reaches all newsroom agents. Integrate existing context packs, mission and site-specific policy without requiring publications to restate universal defaults. Decide which checks are advisory or gates rather than assuming a new blocking gate.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Ryan 2026-11-07: claimed and in progress. Each Story gets four separate checklist items, one per lens (people, AI reader agents, search crawlers, social previews), in the per-Story editorial checklist shown as Kanbus sub-tasks (branch feat/story-checklist). Done needs a findings note; skipped or not applicable needs a reason; an open lens step blocks publishing. Next in this issue: what each lens checks, and the final approval.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Steps 1 and 2 of the four-lens review are merged to develop: the lens definitions and agent context layer (AnthusAI/Papyrus#1281) and the lens-check command with the shared share-preview function (#1284). lens-check reads the four review sub-tasks from the Story checklist (#1282). Still to build, from the design in the agent's report: model-judged checks, stored evidence, enforcing 'cannot close as done' for the three error checks, the final review panel with approval, site policy lines, and post-publish checks. Ryan's answers are recorded in the story-checklist notes.
